text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
VEGOIL SALES - Pakistan bought 6,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil at $545.90 a tonne c and f for shipment by December 31.
SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea will invite tenders for 55,000 T No. 1 soybeans on December 4 for December-January shipment.

WHEAT TENDERS - Turkey will invite bids on December 10 in a tender to import 200,000 T red and white milling wheat on a three-year credit basis, a grain official said on Friday. He said the imports would be made from either the United States, Australia, Argentina or any European Union member country.
- Moroccan millers passed on a tender for 20,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat for delivery between Dec 20 and 30.

WHEAT TENDERS - Taiwan is expected to tender for 72,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat next week. The first shipment of 34,000 tonnes would be delivered from December 15 from U.S. Gulf. The second shipment of 38,000 tonnes would be from December 30, U.S. Gulf. No exact date has been determined.

- Pakistan issued separate tenders on Saturday for 225,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat and Australian white milling wheat for delivery between December 11 and 31. The ministry invited bids on December 1.

WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - Bangladesh has tendered for 200,000 tonnes of U.S. grade-2 wheat for shipment in January and February, food ministry officials said. They said the ministry would receive offers until 0600 GMT on November 30. The shipment for the first 100,000 tonnes should be completed by January 10 and the rest by February 10. The results of the bids will not be known until Dec 3.

BARLEY TENDER - Cyprus on Wednesday invited tenders for the supply of 25,000 tonnes feed barley with a shipment date December 1996 or January 1997. Tenders close on December 3, a statement from the Cyprus Grain Commission said.
LENTIL TENDER - Syria offered 9,500 tonnes of lentils for export. December 16 was set as the final date for bids and results will be announced on December 17.

Market Talk - Turkey, which hopes to get a big share in supplying Iraq's needs under the U.N. oil-for-food deal, said Iraq was expected to import wheat worth $306 million and sugar worth $115 million. The foreign trade undersecretariat (DTM) said in a note to Turkish exporters that Iraq would also buy liquid food oil worth $111 million, rice worth $105 million, lentils $102 million, tea $32 million, milk powder $29 million and $5 million of other food items.

... USDA said ot released an additional $50 million in short-term GSM-102 export credit guarantees to Pakistan for fiscal 1997. It also offered $5 million in intermediate-term GSM-103 export credit guarantees for the sale of breeder livestock in Peru.

... European grain exporters said on Friday that unless the EU starts competing against cheaper wheatsupplies from Argentina, Australia and Canada, it could lose some traditional markets. They particularly fear competition from Argentine wheat which is already making headway in eastern Europe and north Africa, traditional outlets for the EU.
... China has stopped issuing quotas for wheat imports following a bumper grain harvest and may not reconsider wheat import quotas until April 1997, traders in Hong Kong, China and Singapore said.
... About 100,000 tonnes of US soybeans is expected to arrive at Thai ports between December and early January, trade and shipping sources said.
... Bulgaria is expected to call a grain import tender for 300,000 tonnes wheat among seven leading international grain trading companies, its trade minister said.
